questions.question: Why does `const list = []; list.push(1);` run without error, even though `list` is declared with `const`?
options: `const` only prevents reassigning the variable's binding; `push` changes the array's contents, not the binding
`const` arrays are automatically converted to `let` when you call a method on them
`push` is a special method that is allowed to override `const`
It actually throws an error, because `const` freezes the array completely
questions.explanation: `const` only stops you from repointing the label, like `list = somethingElse`; mutating the array's contents with `push` is still allowed.

questions.question: What does `const f = (x) => { x * 2 };` return when called with `5`?
options: undefined
It throws a syntax error
questions.explanation: The curly braces make the body a block, so without an explicit `return x * 2;` the function returns `undefined`.

questions.question: What is the difference between `document.querySelector(".day")` and `document.querySelectorAll(".day")`?
options: `querySelector` searches the head while `querySelectorAll` searches the body
They are identical; `querySelectorAll` is just an alias
`querySelector` returns the first matching element (or null); `querySelectorAll` returns a list of all matches
`querySelector` returns all matches while `querySelectorAll` returns only the first
questions.explanation: `querySelector` returns the first matching element (or null), while `querySelectorAll` returns a list of all matches that you loop over.

questions.question: You want a day button to look 'done' when clicked and 'not done' when clicked again. Which `classList` method does that in one line?
options: `element.classList.add("done")`
`element.classList.remove("done")`
`element.classList.replace("done")`
`element.classList.toggle("done")`
questions.explanation: `classList.toggle("done")` adds the class if it is absent and removes it if present, flipping the state in one line.

questions.question: In the Habit Tracker, why can't you attach a click listener directly to a delete button for a habit that hasn't been created yet?
options: There is no element to attach to yet, so you delegate by listening on a parent that exists and catch the click as it bubbles up
New buttons are read-only until the page is refreshed
Listeners can only be attached inside the `<head>` before the body loads
JavaScript caps the number of listeners, so new buttons are skipped
questions.explanation: The button object doesn't exist yet, so event delegation listens on an always-present parent and handles the click when it bubbles up from the later-added child.

questions.question: You want to delete the habit with `id === 3` from a `habits` array of objects without mutating the original. Which array method fits?
options: `map`, because it transforms each habit into a new one
`forEach`, because it runs a function on every item
`filter`, keeping every habit whose id is not 3 in a new array
`find`, because it returns the first matching habit
questions.explanation: `habits.filter((h) => h.id !== 3)` keeps every habit except the one being deleted and returns a new array, leaving the original untouched.

questions.question: Why do habits need `JSON.stringify` and `JSON.parse` when saving to and loading from localStorage?
options: localStorage only holds strings, so `stringify` packs the array into a string and `parse` unpacks it back into a real array
They encrypt the data so other sites can't read it
They are only needed for numbers, not arrays or objects
localStorage requires every value to be a number, which JSON provides
questions.explanation: localStorage can only store strings, so `JSON.stringify` packs the array into a string to save and `JSON.parse` unpacks it back into a real array on load.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is a promise in JavaScript?
options: A function that always runs before the rest of the page loads
A placeholder for a value that isn't ready yet but will be (or will fail) later
A guaranteed value that fetch returns immediately and directly
A special kind of loop that repeats until data arrives
questions.explanation: A promise is an IOU for a value that arrives later (or fails), which is why you `await` things like `fetch` instead of getting data directly.
